items.meaning: Writing a whole number as a product of only prime numbers

steps: 1. Prime Number: Has exactly two factors (1 and itself, e.g. 2, 3, 5, 7, 11)
2. Split composite number into factor pairs until every branch ends in a prime
3. Write final product using exponents in ascending order (e.g. 60 = 2² × 3 × 5)

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Trophy Case Display
revealWordProblem.text: The school trophy case has 84 trophies to arrange on shelves. The display designer wants to break 84 down into its prime factors first, then use those primes to decide how many equal-sized groups of trophies she can create. What is the prime factorization of 84, written both as a product of primes and using exponents? Show each step of your factor tree.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 84 = 2 × 42. Since 42 is not prime, split it: 42 = 2 × 21. Since 21 is not prime, split it: 21 = 3 × 7. Both 3 and 7 are prime, so the tree is done. The prime factorization of 84 is 2 × 2 × 3 × 7, which can be written with exponents as 2² × 3 × 7. Check: 2 × 2 × 3 × 7 = 4 × 3 × 7 = 12 × 7 = 84. Correct.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 17 has exactly two factors: 1 and 17. 15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7, and 9 = 3 × 3, so they are all composite.
choiceFeedback: 9 splits into 3 × 3, which gives it a third factor besides 1 and 9. Keep checking each number for a hidden factor pair.
15 = 3 × 5, so it has factors besides 1 and itself. A prime number has exactly two factors — test whether any smaller number divides your choice evenly.
21 breaks apart into 3 × 7, so it has more than two factors. Look for the number that can only be divided by 1 and itself.
hints: Re-read what 'prime' means: exactly two factors, 1 and itself. Any extra factor makes a number composite.
Test each choice by dividing by small primes like 2, 3, 5, and 7. If anything divides in evenly, that number is composite.
Start with 9: since 3 × 3 = 9, it has a factor besides 1 and 9, so 9 is composite. Cross it off and test the next choice the same way.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál de los siguientes es un número primo?
questions.explanationEs: 17 tiene exactamente dos factores: 1 y 17. 15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7 y 9 = 3 × 3, así que todos son compuestos.
hintsEs: Relee qué significa 'primo': exactamente dos factores, el 1 y él mismo. Cualquier factor de más vuelve compuesto al número.
Prueba cada opción dividiendo entre primos pequeños como 2, 3, 5 y 7. Si alguno divide exacto, ese número es compuesto.
Empieza con el 9: como 3 × 3 = 9, tiene un factor además del 1 y el 9, así que el 9 es compuesto. Táchalo y prueba la siguiente opción igual.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorization of 30?
questions.explanation: 30 = 2 × 15 = 2 × 3 × 5. All three factors (2, 3, 5) are prime, so 2 × 3 × 5 is the prime factorization.
choiceFeedback: You started the factor tree correctly, but 15 is not prime — it still splits into 3 × 5. Keep going until every branch ends in a prime.
This is a real factor pair of 30, but 10 is composite (10 = 2 × 5). A prime factorization can only contain prime factors.
That is what you get if you stopped too early — 6 is not prime, it still breaks down into 2 x 3 — re-read what the question is asking for.
hints: A prime factorization uses ONLY prime numbers. Look at each choice: are ALL of its factors prime?
Break 30 down step by step, and keep splitting any factor that is still composite until every factor is prime.
Start with 30 = 2 × 15. Is 15 prime? No — so split 15 into two primes and collect everything you found.
questions.explanationEs: 30 = 2 × 15 = 2 × 3 × 5. Los tres factores (2, 3 y 5) son primos, por eso 2 × 3 × 5 es la factorización prima.
hintsEs: Una factorización prima usa SOLO números primos. Mira cada opción: ¿son primos TODOS sus factores?
Descompón el 30 paso a paso y sigue partiendo cualquier factor que todavía sea compuesto hasta que todos los factores sean primos.
Empieza con 30 = 2 × 15. ¿Es primo el 15? No — así que parte el 15 en dos primos y reúne todo lo que encontraste.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorization of 18?
questions.explanation: 18 = 2 × 9 = 2 × 3 × 3. Both 2 and 3 are prime, so 2 × 3 × 3 is the prime factorization.
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you stopped too early — 9 is not prime, it still breaks down into 3 x 3 — re-read what the question is asking for.
3 is prime, but 6 is not — it still splits into 2 × 3. Keep breaking down the composite factor.
Changing the order does not fix the problem: 6 is still composite (6 = 2 × 3). Every factor in the final answer must be prime.
hints: Check every factor in each choice — numbers like 9 and 6 are composite, so they can't appear in a prime factorization.
Build a factor tree for 18: split it into two factors, then keep splitting anything composite until only primes remain.
Begin with 18 = 2 × 9. The 9 isn't prime, so break 9 into two equal prime factors and list all the primes you end with.
questions.explanationEs: 18 = 2 × 9 = 2 × 3 × 3. Tanto 2 como 3 son primos, por eso 2 × 3 × 3 es la factorización prima.
hintsEs: Revisa cada factor de cada opción — números como el 9 y el 6 son compuestos, así que no pueden aparecer en una factorización prima.
Arma un árbol de factores para el 18: pártelo en dos factores y sigue partiendo lo compuesto hasta que solo queden primos.
Comienza con 18 = 2 × 9. El 9 no es primo, así que parte el 9 en dos factores primos iguales y escribe todos los primos con los que terminas.

steps: 1. Prime Number: Has exactly two factors (1 and itself, e.g. 2, 3, 5, 7, 11)
2. Split composite number into factor pairs until every branch ends in a prime
3. Write final product using exponents in ascending order (e.g. 60 = 2² × 3 × 5)
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Prime Factorization is stopping the factor tree too soon — leaving a composite number like 4, 6, 8, or 9 in the final answer instead of continuing to split it. For example, writing 20 = 4 × 5 as the prime factorization (4 is composite) instead of finishing with 20 = 2 × 2 × 5. Before you submit, check every number in your final answer: if any factor can still be broken into smaller factors, the tree isn't finished yet.

hints: Start with 20 = 4 × 5. Then split 4.
hintsEs: Empieza con 20 = 4 × 5. Luego separa 4.
level1.explanation: Split 20 into two factors: 20 = 4 × 5 Split 4 into primes: 4 = 2 × 2 → 20 = 2 × 2 × 5
level1.explanationEs: Separa 20 en dos factores: 20 = 4 × 5 Separa 4 en números primos: 4 = 2 × 2 → 20 = 2 × 2 × 5

hintsEs: Empieza con 66 = 6 × 11. Luego separa 6.

level1.explanationEs: Separa 66 en dos factores: 66 = 6 × 11 Separa 6 en números primos: 6 = 2 × 3 → 66 = 2 × 3 × 11

level1.explanationEs: Separa 27 en dos factores: 27 = 3 × 9 Separa 9 en números primos: 9 = 3 × 3 → 27 = 3 × 3 × 3

level1.stem: Make a factor tree for 48. How many 2s are in its prime factorization?
level1.stemEs: Haz un árbol de factores para 48. ¿Cuántos 2 hay en su factorización prima?
hints: Start with 48 = 6 × 8. Keep splitting until every branch is prime. Then count the 2s.
hintsEs: Empieza con 48 = 6 × 8. Sigue separando hasta que cada rama sea prima. Luego cuenta los 2.
level1.explanation: Split 48 into two factors: 48 = 6 × 8 Split 6 and 8 into primes: 6 = 2 × 3 → 8 = 2 × 2 × 2 Write all the primes. Count the 2s: 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2⁴ × 3
level1.explanationEs: Separa 48 en dos factores: 48 = 6 × 8 Separa 6 y 8 en números primos: 6 = 2 × 3 → 8 = 2 × 2 × 2 Escribe todos los primos. Cuenta los 2: 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2⁴ × 3

level2.stem: Kai says the prime factorization of 24 is 2 × 3 × 4. He is not done. Which of his factors is not prime?
level2.stemEs: Kai dice que la factorización prima de 24 es 2 × 3 × 4. No ha terminado. ¿Cuál de sus factores no es primo?
hints: A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. Test each factor.
hintsEs: Un número primo tiene exactamente dos factores, 1 y él mismo. Prueba cada factor.
level2.explanation: Check each factor: 2 prime → 3 prime → 4 = 2 × 2 Split 4 and write the answer: 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2³ × 3
level2.explanationEs: Revisa cada factor: 2 primo → 3 primo → 4 = 2 × 2 Separa 4 y escribe la respuesta: 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2³ × 3

level2.stem: Find the prime factorization of 54. What is the exponent on 3?
level2.stemEs: Halla la factorización prima de 54. ¿Cuál es el exponente del 3?
hints: Start with 54 = 2 × 27. Then keep splitting 27.
hintsEs: Empieza con 54 = 2 × 27. Luego sigue separando 27.
level2.explanation: Split 54 into two factors: 54 = 2 × 27 Split 27 until every branch is prime: 27 = 3 × 9 → 9 = 3 × 3 Write the primes with exponents: 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 2 × 3³
level2.explanationEs: Separa 54 en dos factores: 54 = 2 × 27 Separa 27 hasta que cada rama sea prima: 27 = 3 × 9 → 9 = 3 × 3 Escribe los primos con exponentes: 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 2 × 3³

hints: Start with 50 = 5 × 10. Then split 10.
hintsEs: Empieza con 50 = 5 × 10. Luego separa 10.
level2.explanation: Split 50 into two factors: 50 = 5 × 10 Split 10, because 10 is not prime: 10 = 2 × 5 → 50 = 2 × 5 × 5
level2.explanationEs: Separa 50 en dos factores: 50 = 5 × 10 Separa 10, porque 10 no es primo: 10 = 2 × 5 → 50 = 2 × 5 × 5

level2.stem: A number has the prime factorization 2² × 3 × 5². What is the number?
level2.stemEs: Un número tiene la factorización prima 2² × 3 × 5². ¿Cuál es el número?
hints: Each exponent tells how many times to use that prime. Write them all, then multiply.
hintsEs: Cada exponente dice cuántas veces se usa ese primo. Escríbelos todos y luego multiplica.
level2.explanation: Write each power as a product: 2² = 4 → 5² = 25 Multiply all the factors: 4 × 3 × 25 = 300
level2.explanationEs: Escribe cada potencia como un producto: 2² = 4 → 5² = 25 Multiplica todos los factores: 4 × 3 × 25 = 300

level2.stem: A store packs 2 × 3² × 7 apples in one box. How many apples are in the box?
level2.stemEs: Una tienda empaca 2 × 3² × 7 manzanas en una caja. ¿Cuántas manzanas hay en la caja?
hints: 3² means 3 × 3. Write all the primes, then multiply.
hintsEs: 3² significa 3 × 3. Escribe todos los primos y luego multiplica.
level2.explanation: Write the exponent as factors: 2 × 3² × 7 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 7 Multiply: 2 × 9 × 7 = 126
level2.explanationEs: Escribe el exponente como factores: 2 × 3² × 7 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 7 Multiplica: 2 × 9 × 7 = 126

level3.stem: What is the prime factorization of 72?
choiceFeedback: The exponents are swapped: four times twenty-seven is 108. Seventy-two holds three 2s and two 3s.
12 is not prime. Keep factoring it into 2 times 2 times 3.
Both factors are right but neither is prime. Break 8 into three 2s and 9 into two 3s.
level3.explanation: A factor tree for 72 ends in the primes 2, 2, 2, 3, and 3. Written with exponents in ascending order, that is 2³ × 3², and 8 × 9 = 72 confirms the value.

level3.stem: Ben says 3² × 5 and 3 × 5² are the same number because they use the same primes. Find 3 × 5².
level3.stemEs: Ben dice que 3² × 5 y 3 × 5² son el mismo número porque usan los mismos primos. Halla 3 × 5².
hints: 5² means 5 × 5. Then multiply by 3.
hintsEs: 5² significa 5 × 5. Luego multiplica por 3.

level3.stem: Find the prime factorization of 150. What is the exponent on 5?
level3.stemEs: Halla la factorización prima de 150. ¿Cuál es el exponente del 5?
hints: Start with 150 = 10 × 15. Split until every branch is prime.
hintsEs: Empieza con 150 = 10 × 15. Separa hasta que cada rama sea prima.
level3.explanation: Split 150 into two factors: 150 = 10 × 15 Split 10 and 15 into primes: 10 = 2 × 5 → 15 = 3 × 5 Write the primes with exponents: 150 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 5 = 2 × 3 × 5²
level3.explanationEs: Separa 150 en dos factores: 150 = 10 × 15 Separa 10 y 15 en números primos: 10 = 2 × 5 → 15 = 3 × 5 Escribe los primos con exponentes: 150 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 5 = 2 × 3 × 5²

level3.stem: A bead store has 2³ × 3 × 5 beads. Each bag holds 2² × 3 beads. How many bags can the store fill?
level3.stemEs: Una tienda tiene 2³ × 3 × 5 cuentas. Cada bolsa tiene capacidad para 2² × 3 cuentas. ¿Cuántas bolsas puede llenar la tienda?
hints: Find each number from its primes. Then divide.
hintsEs: Halla cada número a partir de sus primos. Luego divide.
level3.explanation: Find the number of beads: 2³ × 3 × 5 = 8 × 3 × 5 = 120 Find the beads in one bag: 2² × 3 = 4 × 3 = 12 Divide: 120 ÷ 12 = 10
level3.explanationEs: Halla el número de cuentas: 2³ × 3 × 5 = 8 × 3 × 5 = 120 Halla las cuentas de una bolsa: 2² × 3 = 4 × 3 = 12 Divide: 120 ÷ 12 = 10

level3.stem: A number has only 2s and 3s in its prime factorization. It has at least one of each. The number is between 100 and 110. What is it?
level3.stemEs: Un número tiene solo 2 y 3 en su factorización prima. Tiene al menos uno de cada uno. El número está entre 100 y 110. ¿Cuál es?
hints: Try products like 2 × 3 × 3 × 3. Change how many 2s and 3s you use.
hintsEs: Prueba productos como 2 × 3 × 3 × 3. Cambia cuántos 2 y cuántos 3 usas.
level3.explanation: Try different powers of 2 and 3: 2⁵ × 3 = 96; 2³ × 3² = 72 Find one between 100 and 110: 2² × 3³ = 4 × 27 = 108
level3.explanationEs: Prueba distintas potencias de 2 y de 3: 2⁵ × 3 = 96; 2³ × 3² = 72 Halla uno entre 100 y 110: 2² × 3³ = 4 × 27 = 108
